text.p: Featherlite Mfg Inc, which makes specialty trailers, luxury motor coaches and race car transports, said Tuesday it has locked in substantially all of its expected aluminum costs for 1997 at a price 10 percent less than the average paid in 1996.
The costs for 1997 are 16 percent less than in 1995, it said.
"Continued decreases in the average cost of aluminum will have a positive impact on gross margins," Conrad Clement, president, said in a statement.

Clement said he expects sales to remain strong in all product groups in 1997. "The fundamentals in the niches we are focusing on are positive," he said. "Entertainment and leisure markets are growing and cattle prices have improved."
He added that the company's recently completed acquisition of Vantare, which converts luxury custom coaches, will contribute to the top and bottom lines for a full year in 1997.
"We expect to add significant luxury motorcoach sales in 1997," Clement said.
Featherlite said its sales backlog as of December 31 was $28 million, including $16 million in Vantare orders. A year earlier, its backog was $7.2 milion.
Featherlite today reported higher 1996 fourth quarter and full year results.

It said sales increases for the year were driven by gains in excess of 60 percent in utility and recreational trailers, a 30.8 percent rise in livestock trailers, and 23.8 percent growth in horse trailers.
It said its 1996 gross margin of 14.8 percent was lower than 1995's 15.2 percent, reflecting the increased material cost of luxury motorcoaches.
